html:
SMTO-GML-0047 — Gmail couldn't find the item SMTO asked for

GUID: 33221ac7-6525-4121-bf95-f775e39093db
Slug: gmail-object-not-found
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO asked Gmail for something, such as an email or a setting, that Gmail says doesn't exist in this account. It may have been deleted, moved or belong to a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail in your browser, signed in to the account the Task used, and check that the email, draft, label or setting still exists and isn't in Trash. Gmail reports this when the item was deleted or changed after SMTO last saw it.
  2. If you have more than one Gmail account in SMTO, name the right one in your request, for example 'in @work_gmail'. An item from one account can't be found in another account.
  3. Ask SMTO to search for the item again, for example 'Find the latest email from alice@example.com', then ask it to continue with that result. A fresh search gives SMTO the item's current reference instead of an outdated one.
  4. Before asking for any change again, check Gmail to see whether that change already happened. Earlier steps of the same Task may have finished, and repeating them could change things twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the item and finishes your request without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a short description of the item you meant, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't set SMTO to repeat the request over and over.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail API returned 404 for a provider call whose method name matches no specific resource (message, thread, draft, label, filter, attachment), so GmailService._call raised gmail_object_not_found.

What this means

  • The service wrapper maps provider status 404 to an object/resource-specific missing category according to the called method. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The service wrapper maps provider status 404 to an object/resource-specific missing category according to the called method.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation-specific object type and exact account/resource ID.

How to fix it

  • Re-list the relevant resource on the same account (search, threads, drafts, labels, filters or settings) and use the current ID returned there; a stale or cross-account ID will keep returning 404. Inspect the copied provider_status and method in the error details before reissuing any write.
  • Refresh the relevant mailbox listing and use the current message, thread, draft or label ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Current authorized mailbox discovery supplies the intended existing object reference.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
